description: The settings in Pitwall's ui.json (~/.pitwall/ui.json; $PITWALL_HOME/ui.json). Pitwall applies edits live; an invalid value is reported and the last good one kept. The file also holds spaces and layouts, which are not described here. `pitwall settings list` shows every setting, including the ones kept outside this file.

agentsEditFiles.description: `agents.editFiles`: You can edit text files in Pitwall's file viewer for quick fixes and save them with Cmd+S / Ctrl+S: files of agents on this computer and folders on it, UTF-8 and up to 2 MiB, and an SVG's source. Files of agents on other machines, other images, binary files (PDFs too) and larger files stay read-only. Only you save: agents can't write through Pitwall, and nothing is sent to them. false: the viewer is read-only.

agentsShowDevice.description: `agents.showDevice`: Agents can show you a device's screen in Pitwall when you ask to see the app on a simulator or an emulator ("show me on the simulator"): the `show_device` tool of Pitwall's `pitwall` MCP server (the agents that get it for files get this too), and `pitwall open --device` from a shell. The iOS Simulator, Android emulator or phone opens in a device tile next to the agent's terminal; one still booting is waited for up to a minute. The agent gets nothing back from the screen and can't tap or type in it. Needs general.devicePreviews. false: the tool is gone from the agents' list and `pitwall open --device` refuses.

agentsShowFiles.description: `agents.showFiles`: Agents can show you files, folders and images in Pitwall's file viewer when you ask them to: Pitwall gives the agents it starts its `pitwall` MCP server per launch where the tool has a way (Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, Amp, opencode; your own config files are never edited), Aider gets a rule to run `pitwall-cli open`, and `pitwall open` does the same from a shell. Gemini CLI and Cursor Agent only read their own MCP files: see agents.showFilesGemini and agents.showFilesCursor. false: agents start without it and `pitwall open` refuses. Applies when an agent starts.

agentsShowSettings.description: `agents.showSettings`: Agents can show you Pitwall's Settings at a page when you ask them to ("where do I turn that on", "show me that extension's permissions"): the `show_settings` tool of Pitwall's `pitwall` MCP server (the agents that get it for files get this too), and `pitwall open --settings` from a shell. Settings opens in its tile next to the agent's terminal, or wherever you keep that tile; it never takes the keyboard or brings Pitwall forward. The agent gets nothing back about what Settings holds and can't change, click or type anything in it. false: the tool is gone from the agents' list and `pitwall open --settings` refuses.

agentsShowWeb.description: `agents.showWeb`: Agents can show you a web page in Pitwall when you ask them to ("open the docs on the left", "open a browser window"): the `show_web` tool of Pitwall's `pitwall` MCP server (the agents that get it for files get this too), and `pitwall open --web` from a shell. The page opens in a web tile next to the agent's terminal or a window of its own, in the project's browser account in Pitwall, where you may be signed in; only http and https addresses, shown in the address field. The agent gets nothing back from the page and can't click or type in it. Needs general.webPages. false: the tool is gone from the agents' list and `pitwall open --web` refuses.

density.description: `appearance.density`: Smallest tile before extra agents fold into chips (spaces may override it).

deviceAutoOpen.description: `general.deviceAutoOpen`: When an agent starts an iOS Simulator or an Android emulator (or a phone comes online while it installs an app): beside opens the device's screen in a tile next to that agent's terminal; offer only says so, with Open in Pitwall; off does neither (the device is still in Open device… in the command palette). A device Pitwall can't tie to one agent is only offered. Pitwall looks only while an agent runs a tool that starts devices (simctl, xcodebuild, flutter, expo, react-native, emulator, adb, gradle's install tasks) or prints that it does; it never starts adb's server to look. Needs general.devicePreviews.

devicePreviews.description: `general.devicePreviews`: Device screens in Pitwall: an Android emulator's or phone's screen, or an iOS Simulator's, in a tile of the layout next to your terminals (Open device… in the command palette), where you can tap and type into it. Android needs adb and scrcpy-server; iOS Simulators need Xcode, and touch goes through Xcode's own simulator frameworks in a helper process. Agents can't see or use these screens. false: no device tile opens and none is offered.

engineerAgent.description: `engineer.agent`: What the Race Engineer (Pitwall's optional assistant) runs on: auto (Claude Code if installed, else the first installed agent), an agent id from New agent (claude, codex, gemini, opencode, aider, …) or custom (engineer.command). Applies the next time it starts.

engineerCommand.description: `engineer.command`: The command the Race Engineer runs when engineer.agent is custom (a command line, run by your login shell).

engineerGreeting.default: Introduce yourself in two lines and offer: set up agw, arrange spaces, create agents per project, set up rules, set up an extension, tune settings.
engineerGreeting.description: `engineer.greeting`: The first prompt a new Race Engineer gets, sent when it is first free (empty: none).

actionAccounts.description: The tools' accounts (their ids in accounts.json) each recorded setup action went through without a failure, by the same keys as `actionSteps`. A step for a tool runs for its default folder and for each Pitwall account of it; the action counts as done only once every current account of its tools is here. A record without an entry, from before accounts were kept, covers none.

steps.description: A digest of the steps confirmed, as in `actionSteps`.

actionConfirmed.description: The steps of each setup action the user confirmed, by the same keys as `actionSteps`: Pitwall runs exactly those, by itself, for a tool's account added later (or not yet covered), while the extension is on. Once the steps change (an update), nothing runs until the user confirms them again.

actionSteps.description: A digest of the steps each recorded setup action ran, by action (`<action>@<connection>` for one kept per connection): when an update changes an action's steps, its step is unticked and asks to be run again.

actionsDone.description: Its setup actions that last ran without a failure (their steps in Settings stay ticked); one that uses a setting is kept per connection, this list copying the carried-over connection's.

connection.description: The connection its inbox lists, by id (absent: all of them). One that is gone, or a single connection, lists all.

devPath.description: A development folder it is loaded from, where it is (Settings → Extensions → Load from folder…): used instead of an installed copy, never copied or changed by Pitwall. Removing it from the list forgets this, never the folder.

enabled.description: The extension is on: its adapter runs and its inbox can be opened.

at.description: When the user answered, in seconds since 1970 (UTC).

grants.description: The user's answer to each permission it asks for (docs/extensions/permissions.md), by name, with when. One it asks for without an answer here (added by an update) is not granted. Turning a grant off applies to its next call.

lastUpdate.description: Its last update (docs/extensions/updates.md): Go back offers to put back the data backup taken then.

backup.description: The backup folder of its service's data taken before it (under extension-backups/<id>/).

confirmed.description: A digest of its service's commands as confirmed before the update: Go back confirms them again.

from.description: The version it was updated from.

to.description: The version it was updated to.

restartAfterUpdate.description: Overrides `extensionsRestartAfterUpdate` for this extension: what Pitwall does with running agents that use its previous setup after an update.

secretsSet.description: A copy of which secrets that connection has set, for an older Pitwall. The secrets are in the system's secure store, never in this file.

selected.description: The thread its inbox tile shows (`<connection id>:<thread>` for an extension with connections).

service.description: Its service, the program Pitwall keeps running while it is on (docs/extensions/service.md).

confirmed.description: The commands the user confirmed. Pitwall starts it only while its commands are these: an update that changes them stops it and asks again.

digest.description: A digest of its commands as the user confirmed them.

fresh.description: Its data folder was empty when Pitwall started it and its first run (a first sign-in) hasn't succeeded since: the first run is offered.

stopped.description: The user stopped it: it isn't started until they press Start.

values.description: A copy of the plain settings of the connection carried over from before connections, for an older Pitwall (the settings live in accounts.json).

viewWindows.description: Its views (by id) in windows of their own, each opened again at the next start; a view tile in a layout is a pane's `view` (`<extension>/<view>`).

window.description: Its inbox is in a window of its own, opened again at the next start (one inbox per extension, whichever connections it shows).

extensions.description: Extensions (Settings → Extensions): one entry per extension id, with `enabled` (default false: an extension found in the extensions folder of Pitwall's data folder is off until you turn it on). An extension that is on runs an adapter per connection; `selected` is the thread its inbox tile shows, `actionsDone` its setup actions that ran without a failure. An extension's settings live in its connections (accounts of kind `ext:<id>` in `accounts.json`, one per server or key; secrets in the system's secure store, never in a file); `values` and `secretsSet` here are a copy of the connection carried over from before connections, kept for an older Pitwall. Not a `pitwall settings` key: turn extensions on and off in Settings or here.

extensionsRestartAfterUpdate.description: `extensions.restartAfterUpdate`: After an extension's update, what Pitwall does with running agents that use its previous setup (docs/extensions/updates.md): ask (restart nothing; their rows say so, with Restart), whenIdle (restart each once it has waited for you for 30 s, one at a time, continuing its conversation; never one that is working, waiting on an approval or can't continue its conversation) or never. An extension's card can override it.

floatingPrompts.description: `general.floatingPrompts`: While Pitwall isn't in front and an agent needs you, show a small floating control above other apps, on every desktop: who waits and what it wants, one prompt at a time and oldest first, with Accept and Reject for a plain yes/no prompt and Open for everything else, and the open questions in the inboxes of extensions that are on, answered right there. Resize it by any edge or corner.

fontSize.description: `appearance.terminalFontSize`: Base terminal font size in px; tiles may shrink below it to fit.

hideElsewhere.description: The inverse of `general.showElsewhere`: Show agents running in other terminal apps as a sidebar group (read-only, checked every ~10 s).

look.description: `appearance.look`: Flat, or Glass: translucent chrome over the window material (Liquid Glass where the OS has it). Terminals stay solid.

noToolUpdates.description: The inverse of `agents.updateTools`: Pitwall keeps agent tools up to date itself (claude update, at startup and every 6 hours, one at a time) and turns off their own updaters in what it starts, so many sessions don't update at once and break the install. false: each tool updates itself.

reduceMotion.description: `appearance.reduceMotion`: Fewer animations (the OS setting also applies).

sidebarGroup.description: `general.sidebarGroup`: How the sidebar groups agents: by project, or by account (the Claude Code or Codex login they run on; by profile once you have one), then project.

theme.description: `appearance.theme`: Light or dark; system follows the OS.

webPages.description: `general.webPages`: Web pages in Pitwall: a page in a tile of the layout next to your terminals (Cmd+L / Ctrl+Shift+L, or Open web page… in the command palette), and an agent's Preview of the dev server its terminal printed, in the system's own web view. Pages keep their logins in Pitwall's own browser accounts, not your browser's. Agents can't see or use these pages; with agents.showWeb they can open one for you to see. false: no web view is made, a Preview opens in your browser instead, and agents can't open pages either.

title: Pitwall settings (ui.json)
